chapters.title: Introduction

sections.title: Getting Started
sections.summary: Installing Lean 4, VS Code and the mathematics_in_lean repository; working from a copy of the exercise files and comparing with the solutions folder.

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: What the book covers and its style: Lean as a language for mathematics, the infoview, and the habit of checking each step interactively.

chapters.summary: How to install Lean, Mathlib and the exercise files, and how the book is meant to be read: with the editor open, doing exercises.

chapters.title: Basics

sections.title: Calculating
sections.summary: Rewriting with rw, chaining equations with calc, and the ring tactic for commutative-ring identities over the reals.

sections.title: Proving Identities in Algebraic Structures
sections.summary: Proving identities from the axioms of a ring or group, with variables and sections, to see what ring automates.

sections.title: Using Theorems and Lemmas
sections.summary: Applying library theorems with apply and exact, inequalities with le_trans and friends, and the linarith, norm_num and positivity tactics; min, max, abs and divisibility.

sections.title: More examples using apply and rw
sections.summary: More practice with apply and rw on min, max, absolute value, gcd and lcm, and on lattices of divisibility.

sections.title: Proving Facts about Algebraic Structures
sections.summary: Proving facts in partial orders, lattices, ordered rings and metric spaces from their axioms; reading Mathlib's class structure.

chapters.summary: Proving things by calculation: rewriting with equations, using library lemmas, and the first look at how algebraic structures are organized.

chapters.title: Logic

sections.title: Implication and the Universal Quantifier
sections.summary: Proving and using ∀ and →: intro, apply, and definitions that unfold to quantified statements, such as bounds and monotonicity.

sections.title: The Existential Quantifier
sections.summary: Proving ∃ with use and using it with rcases or obtain; worked examples with bounds and surjectivity.

sections.title: Negation
sections.summary: Negation as implication to False: by_contra, push_neg, contrapose, absurd and exfalso, and classical reasoning.

sections.title: Conjunction and Iff
sections.summary: Proving and destructuring ∧ and ↔: constructor, anonymous constructor notation, rcases patterns, and iff lemmas in rewriting.

sections.title: Disjunction
sections.summary: Proving ∨ with left and right, case splits with rcases, and excluded middle via by_cases.

sections.title: Sequences and Convergence
sections.summary: Putting it together: the ε–N definition of convergence, uniqueness of limits, and sums and products of convergent sequences.

chapters.summary: The logical connectives as moves in a proof: how to prove and how to use each of ∀, →, ∃, ¬, ∧, ↔ and ∨, ending with limits of sequences.

chapters.title: Sets and Functions

sections.title: Sets
sections.summary: Sets in Mathlib as predicates: membership, subset, intersection, union, complement, set-builder notation and indexed unions and intersections; ext and the mem lemmas.

sections.title: Functions
sections.summary: Images and preimages, injectivity and surjectivity, inverse functions and their construction with choice; Cantor's theorem on surjections to the power set.

sections.title: The Schröder-Bernstein Theorem
sections.summary: A formal proof that injections both ways give a bijection, built by iterating the two maps and choosing on the image.

chapters.summary: Sets as predicates on a type, functions between types, and a full formal proof of the Schröder–Bernstein theorem.

chapters.title: Elementary Number Theory

sections.title: Irrational Roots
sections.summary: Irrationality of √2 and of roots of primes, coprimality, primes, and a counting argument with prime factorizations.

sections.title: Induction and Recursion
sections.summary: Natural numbers as an inductive type; factorial and Fibonacci by recursion; induction proofs; finite sums with Finset.sum_range_succ, including the proof that 1 + ⋯ + n = n(n+1)/2 by doubling and dividing.

sections.title: Infinitely Many Primes
sections.summary: Euclid's proof by factorials and by finite sets; strong induction for prime factors; infinitely many primes congruent to 3 mod 4.

sections.title: More Induction
sections.summary: Further forms of induction: structural recursion with several base cases, strong induction and generalizing the hypothesis, applied to Fibonacci-style definitions.

chapters.summary: Number theory as a testing ground for induction, recursion and finite sums: irrationality, the sum formula, and infinitely many primes.

chapters.title: Discrete Mathematics

sections.title: Finsets and Fintypes
sections.summary: Finite sets (Finset) and finite types (Fintype): operations, filter, image, sums and products, cardinality, and induction over a finset.

sections.title: Counting Arguments
sections.summary: Counting by products, disjoint unions, images and sums; double counting and the pigeonhole principle.

sections.title: Inductively Defined Types
sections.summary: Custom inductive types (lists, binary trees, propositional formulas), defined by structural recursion and reasoned about by induction.

chapters.summary: Finite combinatorics in Mathlib, and how to define and reason about one's own inductive types.

chapters.title: Structures

sections.title: Defining structures
sections.summary: Declaring structures with fields, constructors and projections; extensionality, and proving properties of points and of a standard simplex.

sections.title: Algebraic Structures
sections.summary: Algebraic structures (groups and others) as structures and type classes; instances, and why instance search matters.

sections.title: Building the Gaussian Integers
sections.summary: Defining the Gaussian integers ℤ[i] as a structure, giving it a commutative-ring instance, and proving a Euclidean division property.

chapters.summary: How mathematical objects with several components are defined in Lean: structures, algebraic structures as classes, and a worked example.

chapters.title: Hierarchies

sections.title: Basics
sections.summary: Classes that carry data versus classes that carry properties; extends, to_additive, and forgetful inheritance with default fields to avoid bad diamonds.

sections.title: Morphisms
sections.summary: Morphisms as predicates versus bundled structures; coercion to functions, morphism classes with outParam, and DFunLike.

sections.title: Sub-objects
sections.summary: Sub-objects with SetLike, submonoid classes for shared lemmas, the lattice of sub-objects, and quotients by setoids.

chapters.summary: How Mathlib builds hierarchies of classes without duplication or diamonds, bundles morphisms, and treats sub-objects and quotients.

chapters.title: Groups and Rings

sections.title: Monoids and Groups
sections.summary: Monoids and groups, homomorphisms and isomorphisms, subgroups and lattices of subgroups, concrete groups, group actions, quotient groups, and results such as Lagrange and Sylow.

sections.title: Rings
sections.summary: Rings, units, ring morphisms, ideals and quotients, the Chinese remainder theorem, algebras and polynomials.

chapters.summary: Mathlib's algebra in practice: monoids, groups and their actions, and rings, ideals and polynomials.

chapters.title: Linear algebra

sections.title: Vector spaces and linear maps
sections.summary: Vector spaces as modules over a field; linear maps, their sums and composites, and linear equivalences.

sections.title: Subspaces and quotients
sections.summary: Subspaces, their lattice, images and preimages under linear maps, and quotient spaces.

sections.title: Endomorphisms
sections.summary: Endomorphisms, polynomials applied to them, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and the Cayley–Hamilton theorem.

sections.title: Matrices, bases and dimension
sections.summary: Matrices, bases and coordinates, the matrix of a linear map, and finite dimension and rank.

chapters.summary: Linear algebra as Mathlib states it: modules over a field, maps, subspaces, endomorphisms, and matrices with bases.

chapters.title: Topology

sections.title: Filters
sections.summary: Filters and the Tendsto relation as a single way to talk about limits, neighborhoods and "eventually"; the filter API.

sections.title: Metric spaces
sections.summary: Metric spaces: balls, open and closed sets, continuity, compactness, uniform continuity and completeness.

sections.title: Topological spaces
sections.summary: Topological spaces: neighborhoods, continuity, separation, compactness, and how filters tie these together.

chapters.summary: Topology the Mathlib way: filters as the unifying notion of limit, then metric and general topological spaces.

chapters.title: Differential Calculus

sections.title: Elementary Differential Calculus
sections.summary: Derivatives of real functions: HasDerivAt, deriv, the sum rule, Rolle's theorem and the mean value theorem, and simp for computing derivatives.

sections.title: Differential Calculus in Normed Spaces
sections.summary: Normed spaces and continuous linear maps, the operator norm, big-O and little-o comparisons, the Fréchet derivative, smoothness and the local inverse theorem.

chapters.summary: Derivatives, first for real functions and then for maps between normed spaces.

chapters.title: Integration and Measure Theory

sections.title: Elementary Integration
sections.summary: Interval integrals on the reals, the fundamental theorem of calculus, and convolution.

sections.title: Measure Theory
sections.summary: σ-algebras, measurable sets, measures and outer measures, and "almost everywhere" statements.

sections.title: Integration
sections.summary: The Bochner integral for Banach-space-valued functions, dominated convergence, Fubini, convolution and change of variables.

chapters.summary: Integration on intervals, measure theory, and the general Bochner integral.

title: Mathematics in Lean
byline: Jeremy Avigad and Patrick Massot · current online edition (v4.34.0, 2020–2025, Lean 4 and Mathlib), CC BY 4.0
note: The book is published as a website (with exercise files in the companion repository leanprover-community/mathematics_in_lean), so every section links to its place in the current online edition instead of a PDF page range. The older Lean 3 edition (with Kevin Buzzard and Robert Y. Lewis) is superseded and not broken out. It can also be read with an AI reading companion on [ChapterPal](https://www.chapterpal.com/book/fd356955-a80d-4490-aa0b-b0e01bfe65bb/mathematics-in-lean). Summaries are in our own words.
summary: A hands-on course in formalizing ordinary mathematics in Lean 4 with Mathlib, written for mathematicians rather than programmers. It starts with rewriting and calculation in rings and orders, then teaches the logical connectives as proof moves (intro, apply, rcases, use, by_contra), sets and functions, and elementary number theory with induction and recursion, including the formula 1 + ⋯ + n = n(n+1)/2. The middle chapters treat finite sets and counting, inductive types, and how structures, classes and algebraic hierarchies are designed in Mathlib (bundled morphisms, sub-objects, quotients); later chapters apply all of this to groups and rings, linear algebra, topology through filters, differential calculus in normed spaces, and measure theory and integration. Each section comes with exercises meant to be done in VS Code alongside the text.
